independence_statement: This is a new global polynomial symplectic Hénon candidate selected from Paper 2's integrality obstruction. It does not reopen the branch-baker or one-dimensional derivative-clock candidates and consumes no prime table, Riemann-zero data, or sealed candidate result.
research_question: Can the globally polynomial area-preserving Henon map H_u(X,Y)=(X^2-u-Y,X), at the inherited algebraic-integer PCF parameter u, have a finite complex periodic orbit with a return multiplier of exact rational-prime modulus, without assuming that the multiplier itself is rational?

parameter.provenance: Inherited exactly from the pre-existing PCF parameter used in Papers 1 and 2; not selected by multiplier inspection, prime fitting, zeta zeros, or spectral data.

map.scope: global polynomial automorphism of A^2; no singular branch lift and no compactness claim

definitions.finite_periodic_point: P in A^2(C) with H_u^n(P)=P for some n>=1; the cyclic projective system is frozen to prove P lies in A^2(Qbar)
definitions.cycle_multiplier: an eigenvalue lambda of D_P(H_u^n); exact period is recorded separately
definitions.raw_rational_prime_modulus_target: abs(lambda)=p for a positive rational prime p; lambda need not lie in Q
definitions.exact_rational_modulus_target: abs(lambda)=q in Q_{>0}; q is in scope only as an exact algebraic equality
definitions.rational_modulus_s_unit_target: q=abs(lambda) in Q_{>0} with numerator and denominator supported only on a predeclared finite bad-prime set
definitions.irrational_or_approximate_modulus_target: abs(lambda) not in Q, or only numerically near Q; outside the prime-support conclusion

primary_claims: C1: Every complex periodic coordinate of H_u is algebraic by projective homogenization of the cyclic recurrence, and is an algebraic integer by a non-archimedean cyclic maximum argument.
C2: Every periodic monodromy belongs to SL_2 of the algebraic integers, so both multipliers are algebraic units.

C3: Complex conjugation preserves algebraic units; therefore abs(lambda) in Q implies abs(lambda)=1 for H_u, so no rational-prime multiplier modulus occurs at any period even when lambda is nonrational. Rational lambda=+1 or -1 is a special case.

C4: For finite compositions of monic area-preserving generalized Henon factors over O_{K,S}, complex periodic coordinates are S-integral and any exact rational modulus abs(lambda)=q has prime support only below S. The proof uses a Galois closure and all places above the same rational bad primes, avoiding any conjugation-stability assumption on (K,S).
C5: The rational control a=-15/16 has fixed point (5/4,5/4) and exact multipliers 2 and 1/2, showing that a bad prime inserted in the coefficient denominator can occur in the multiplier.
nonclaims: no obstruction to large or unstable irrational algebraic multiplier moduli

exact rational spectral radius is covered only as a determinant-one two-dimensional corollary of the rational-modulus theorem
no assertion that +1 or -1 occurs or is absent for H_u

theorem_extension.periodic_point_quantifier: finite complex periodic points; cyclic projective homogenization proves algebraicity before valuation arguments
theorem_extension.conjugation_stable_place_set: in a finite Galois M/Q containing lambda, use every place of M above rational primes in S_Q; this set is stable under complex conjugation and has unchanged rational-prime support
theorem_extension.conjugation_logic_boundary: conjugate(lambda) is an S_Q-unit by field automorphism; it is not assumed to equal the reciprocal eigenvalue. Only lambda*conjugate(lambda)=abs(lambda)^2 is used.
theorem_extension.prime_support_conclusion: abs(lambda)=q in Q_{>0} implies q in Z[S_Q^-1]^x; lambda itself need not be rational
theorem_extension.mandatory_boundary: leading coefficients or Jacobian coefficients that are not units must be added to the bad set before the theorem is applied

stop_rules: Any failure of the parameter identity, polynomial inverse, determinant-one identity, or non-archimedean maximum proof is an implementation/theory stop.

A candidate multiplier with exactly rational modulus other than 1 is treated first as an algebra, embedding, conjugation, or period-handling error; the exact theorem must be independently reaudited before any scientific reinterpretation. A rational multiplier outside +1,-1 is a special case.
Formal period is never called exact period until lower-period contamination is excluded.
A finite absence through period 3 must never be reported as evidence for the all-period theorem.

Exact abs(lambda)=q in Q is an in-scope theorem claim, but a displayed floating modulus is never promoted to an exact rational equality. Irrational moduli, singular values, and Lyapunov exponents remain outside scope.

In dimension two with determinant one, an exactly rational spectral radius is reported only as a corollary of the exact rational-modulus result; general or approximate spectral radii are not classified.
The bad-prime set is frozen from coefficient denominators and Jacobian data before multiplier computation; it may not be inferred from observed multipliers.
Passing the theorem and audits closes the rational-prime-modulus clock for this candidate; it does not open prime tables, Riemann zeros, zeta fitting, quantization, or Route B.
